desc:
The degree of an array is the highest number of times any single value occurs in it. For example, the degree of [1, 3, 3, 2, 3, 1] is 3, because the value 3 occurs three times.

Given a non-empty integer array nums, find the shortest contiguous subarray whose degree equals the degree of the whole array, and return its length.
hints: Compute the degree first. Which values reach that frequency?
A shortest valid subarray can always be trimmed so that it starts and ends on an occurrence of a most frequent value.
Record the first index, last index and count of every value in one pass. For each value whose count equals the degree, candidate length is last - first + 1; take the minimum.
editorial: Any subarray with degree equal to the global degree d must contain some value v exactly d times, where v is one of the globally most frequent values. The shortest such window for a fixed v runs from its first occurrence to its last occurrence.
So one pass recording first[v], last[v] and count[v] is enough. The answer is the minimum of last[v] - first[v] + 1 over all values with count[v] equal to the maximum count. The runtime is linear.
